hints: Treat blocks $A$ ($80\text{ kg}$) and $B$ ($40\text{ kg}$) as a single system of mass $120\text{ kg}$ along the $20^\circ$ incline.
Sum forces up the plane: $500\cos 15^\circ - 50 - (80 + 40)g\sin 20^\circ = (80 + 40)a$, and solve for acceleration $a$.
Isolate block $B$: $T - 50 - 40g\sin 20^\circ = 40a$, and substitute the acceleration to find tension $T$.
walkthrough:
Apply Newton's second law along the incline to the combined system of blocks $A$ and $B$:
$$500\cos 15^\circ - 50 - (80 + 40)g\sin 20^\circ = (80 + 40)a$$
$$500\cos 15^\circ - 50 - 1200\sin 20^\circ = 120a$$
$$482.963 - 50 - 410.424 = 120a \implies 22.539 = 120a$$

Solve for the acceleration $a$:
$$a = \frac{22.539}{120} \approx 0.188\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Apply Newton's second law to block $B$ to find tension $T$ in the rope:
$$T - 50 - 40g\sin 20^\circ = 40a$$
$$T = 50 + 400\sin 20^\circ + 40(0.1878) \approx 50 + 136.808 + 7.513 \approx 194\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.Solving Connected-Particle Systems: Applies Newton's second law to obtain acceleration $a = 0.188\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and rope tension $T = 194\text{ N}$.

teacher_walkthrough:
Analyze the connected two-block system moving up the plane inclined at $20^\circ$:
- Block $A$: mass $m_A = 80\text{ kg}$, pulled by $500\text{ N}$ at $15^\circ$ above the slope, no resistance.
- Block $B$: mass $m_B = 40\text{ kg}$, resistance $R_B = 50\text{ N}$.
- Total mass: $M = m_A + m_B = 80 + 40 = 120\text{ kg}$.

Apply Newton's second law along the line of greatest slope to the entire system:
$$\sum F_{\parallel} = M a$$
Forward component of external pulling force:
$$F_{\text{pull},\parallel} = 500\cos 15^\circ \approx 500(0.965926) = 482.963\text{ N}$$
Opposing forces:
- Resistance on $B$: $50\text{ N}$
- Downhill component of total weight: $Mg\sin 20^\circ = (120)(10)\sin 20^\circ = 1200\sin 20^\circ$
$$1200\sin 20^\circ \approx 1200(0.342020) = 410.424\text{ N}$$
Set up the equation:
$$482.963 - 50 - 410.424 = 120a$$
$$22.539 = 120a$$
Divide by $120$:
$$a = \frac{22.539}{120} \approx 0.187825\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $a = 0.188\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

Isolate block $B$ to determine the tension $T$ in the rope:
Block $B$ moves up the slope with acceleration $a = 0.187825\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$\sum F_{\parallel} = m_B a$$
$$T - R_B - m_B g\sin 20^\circ = m_B a$$
Substitute $R_B = 50\text{ N}$, $m_B g\sin 20^\circ = 400\sin 20^\circ \approx 136.808\text{ N}$, and $m_B a = 40(0.187825) \approx 7.513\text{ N}$:
$$T - 50 - 136.808 = 7.513$$
$$T = 50 + 136.808 + 7.513 = 194.321\text{ N}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $T = 194\text{ N}$.

hints: Use the constant-acceleration formula relating $u = 0$, $v = 1.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and acceleration $a = 0.188\text{ m s}^{-2}$: $v = u + at$.
walkthrough:
Apply $v = u + at$ with initial speed $u = 0$, target speed $v = 1.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and acceleration $a = 0.1878\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$v = u + at$$
$$1.2 = 0 + 0.1878t$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Identify the kinematic quantities:
- Initial speed: $u = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ (released from rest)
- Final speed: $v = 1.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$
- Constant acceleration: $a = 0.187825\text{ m s}^{-2}$ (from part (a))
- Time taken: $t$

Select the appropriate suvat equation:
$$v = u + at$$

Divide both sides by $0.187825$:
$$t = \frac{1.2}{0.187825} \approx 6.3889\text{ s}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $t = 6.39\text{ s}$.
